title: Shine Forth, Eternal Source of Light
description: Shine Forth, Eternal Source of Light in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 494 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Knowledge of God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Shine forth, E-ter-nal Source of light! And make thy glo-ries known; Fill our en-larged, a-dor-ing sight With lus-tre all thine own.

lines: Shine forth, Eternal Source of light!
Vain are the charms, and faint the rays
And all their grandeur and their praise
To know the Author of our frame
True science is to read thy name,
True life to obey thy will.
For this I long, for this I pray,

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
